transcript:
[doctor] Hi Jane, good to see you today. I see from your notes that you've been experiencing some fatigue and muscle weakness. Can you tell me more about that?

[patient] Yes, doctor. I've been feeling really tired and weak in my muscles for the past three months. It's been quite persistent.

[doctor] Hmm, I see. On a scale from mild to severe, how would you rate these symptoms?

[patient] I'd say they are mild to moderate. They sometimes get worse, but not unbearable.

[doctor] Alright. Have you noticed any other symptoms along with the fatigue and muscle weakness?

[patient] Yes, occasionally I have bone pain. It flares up every now and then.

[doctor] Okay, how has this been affecting your daily life?

[patient] It's been tough. My energy levels are really low, and it's affecting my productivity and daily tasks.

[doctor] I understand. Have you had any headaches, dizziness, or numbness?

[patient] No, none of those symptoms.

[doctor] Any rashes or skin discolorations?

[patient] No, my skin seems normal.

[doctor] How about any symptoms that might suggest your thyroid is acting up?

[patient] No, nothing different from what I usually experience with my hypothyroidism.

[doctor] Alright, Jane. Can you give me your medical history record?

[patient] Here you are.

[doctor] Thank you. Based on your medical history record, I see you have hypothyroidism and you're stable on your current treatment. When was the last time you had your thyroid function checked?

[patient] It was checked a few months ago, and everything was stable.

[doctor] That's good to hear. Now let's move on to the physical exam. Your vitals look good. Blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 bpm, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, temperature is 98.6°F, and your oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] I'm going to check a few things. Please stay still. Your head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat look normal. There's no nasal congestion or throat abnormalities. Your neck has no lymphadenopathy, goiter, or mass. Your breath sounds are clear bilaterally, no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.

[patient] Alright.

[doctor] Your heart sounds are normal as well, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Your abdomen is soft and non-tender with no hepatosplenomegaly.

[patient] Sounds good so far.

[doctor] I do notice some mild tenderness in your muscles and bones, but otherwise, you have a normal range of motion. There are no rashes, lesions, or skin discolorations. Your neurological exam is normal; you're alert and oriented with no focal deficits.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] Now, let’s discuss your recent blood work. It shows that your 25-hydroxy vitamin D level is low at 18 ng/mL, whereas the normal range is between 30-100 ng/mL.

[patient] Oh, I see.

[doctor] This low vitamin D level could be contributing to your fatigue and muscle weakness. So, my assessment is that you have a vitamin D deficiency.

[patient] What should I do about it?

[doctor] I’m going to prescribe you Vitamin D supplementation: 2000 IU, oral, daily for 3 months.

[patient] Sounds good.

[doctor] Additionally, try to increase your sun exposure to about 15 minutes daily. Adjust your diet to include more vitamin D-rich foods, such as fatty fish and fortified dairy products.

[patient] I can do that.

[doctor] We will re-evaluate your vitamin D levels in 3 months. I will schedule a re-check of your 25-hydroxy vitamin D levels after that period.

[patient] Alright.

[doctor] It’s important that you adhere to the prescribed supplementation and lifestyle modifications. If you experience any new symptoms or signs of vitamin D toxicity, please report them immediately.

[patient] What are the signs of vitamin D toxicity?

[doctor] They include nausea, vomiting, weakness, and frequent urination. But these are rare at the prescribed dosage.

[patient] Got it.

[doctor] Also, continue your current Levothyroxine regimen and monitor your thyroid function as per your endocrinologist's recommendations.

[patient] I will.

[doctor] Do you have any questions or concerns about what we've discussed today?

[patient] No, everything seems clear. Thank you.

[doctor] Great. If you have any concerns before your follow-up, don't hesitate to contact the clinic. I’ll see you in 3 months for a re-evaluation of your vitamin D levels and overall assessment.

[patient] Thank you, doctor.

[doctor] You're welcome, Jane. Take care and see you in 3 months.
